memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord said to Moses, 'Chisel out two stone tablets like the first ones, and I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke. Be ready in the morning, and then come up on Mount Sinai. Present yourself to me there on top of the mountain.'" - Exod 34:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The tablets lie shattered at the foot of the mountain. And God says: bring Me two more.

Think about what God does not say. He does not say the covenant is finished. He does not say Israel has used up its chances. He simply prepares to write the same words again.

That is the character of our God. He is a God of second writings. What we break, He is willing to rewrite. Not because the breaking did not matter — it mattered terribly — but because His purposes are not hostage to our failures.

Notice the small difference this time: Moses must chisel the stone himself, though God still does the writing. There is a cost to restoration, a work of preparation. Grace is free, but it is not casual. God calls Moses to labour through the night and be ready in the morning.

Peter knew this. He denied Christ three times, and the risen Jesus restored him with three questions on a beach (John 21:15-17). The failure was not erased from history, but it did not have the final word.

If something in your life is shattered, hear this: God still writes. Bring Him the pieces.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What in your life feels broken beyond repair?
2. Do you believe God is willing to write again on your life?
3. What preparation might God be calling you to before restoration comes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are a God of second writings. Take what is broken in me and write Your Word there again. Amen.
